To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical Marangani number for buoyancy–thermocopilary convection in volatile liquids increases significantly as the average concentration of non-condensable gas in the gas phase is reduced.

(i) the effect of the gas phase is to reduce the heat transfer from the surface to the gas and to the gas to the surface; (ii) the heat transfer from and to the surface is proportional to the heat transfer from surface to the gas; (iii) the effect of phase change is to increase the heat transfer from to the surface and to the gas; and (iv) the effect of gas phase is to increase the effect of phase-change on the heat transfer.

the effect of the gas phase composition is explained by the fact that the gas phase has an impact on the transport of both heat and vapour and that the effect on heat transport is dominant at atmospheric conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of phase change and gas phase on the stability of convective rolls in a layer of a volatile liquid driven by horizontal temperature gradient.
the effect of phase change and the transport of heat, vapour and air on the stability of a layer of volatile fluid heated from below and cooled from above.
the effect of phase change, and more specifically, the effect of the composition of the gaseous mixture, on the stability and pattern formation in a layer of a volatile liquid heated from below.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of the gas phase on the onset of convective flow is a result of the combined effect of the transport of heat through the gas phase, the phase change and the thermocapillary effect at the liquid–gas interface.
the gas phase has an important effect on the stability of convective flows driven by a horizontal thermal gradient.
the gas phase is a key factor in the onset of convec-tion, which should always be accounted for in modelling of such systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gas phase is not only important for the stability of convection but also for the heat and mass transfer in the layer of liquid.
the effect of the gas phase on the stability of the flow is primarily determined by the ratio of the thermal conductivity to the mass diffusivity in the gas phase, rather than by the phase change.
, when the liquid phase is volatile, the effect of gas phase on the stability and pattern formation of the convective flow is non-trivial and should not be neglected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of the gas phase on convective stability should be taken into consideration in all cases where the gas is not at atmospheric conditions.
the gas-phase effects must be taken into consideration in order to understand and accurately predict the onset of buoyancy–thermally driven convection.
the effect of phase change should be taken into account in studies of thermocapillary convections, even when the gas phase is assumed to be air.
